headline_marked: EC to [[announce UP election schedule this month]]
headline: EC to announce UP election schedule this month
summary: Election Commissioner Anwarul Islam Sarkar says the code of conduct is finalized and preparations for the Union Parishad polls are underway.
details: Election Commissioner (EC) Anwarul Islam Sarkar announced on Sunday that the schedule for the Union Parishad (UP) elections will be released within this month.
During a briefing at the Election Building, he stated that the code of conduct for local government elections has already been finalized.
The EC has completed the updating of voter lists and the determination of polling centers, while the preparation of panels for presiding and assistant presiding officers is currently ongoing.
The Election Commission will hold a review meeting next week specifically regarding the Union Parishad elections.
To ensure a violence-free and neutral election, the EC plans to consult with political parties, law enforcement agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
The commission also plans to increase the number of CCTV cameras and body-worn cameras at polling centers to maintain security and transparency.

Regarding a demand from Jamaat-e-Islami for MPO-listed teachers to participate in the elections, the EC noted that such political involvement by teachers could hinder the fair environment of educational institutions.
caption:
The Union Parishad election schedule is coming this month. The EC has finalized the code of conduct and is ramping up security with more CCTV and body cameras.

Election Commissioner (EC) Anwarul Islam Sarkar announced on Sunday that the schedule for the Union Parishad (UP) elections will be released within this month.

During a briefing at the Election Building, he stated that the code of conduct for local government elections has already been finalized.

The EC has completed the updating of voter lists and the determination of polling centers, while the preparation of panels for presiding and assistant presiding officers is currently ongoing.

The Election Commission will hold a review meeting next week specifically regarding the Union Parishad elections.

To ensure a violence-free and neutral election, the EC plans to consult with political parties, law enforcement agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.

The commission also plans to increase the number of CCTV cameras and body-worn cameras at polling centers to maintain security and transparency.

Regarding a demand from Jamaat-e-Islami for MPO-listed teachers to participate in the elections, the EC noted that such political involvement by teachers could hinder the fair environment of educational institutions.

#Bangladesh #ElectionCommission #UPElections #LocalGovernment #Politics

Source: Jamuna TV

headline_marked: 251 people disappeared: [[ICT begins recording statements from families]]
headline: 251 people disappeared: ICT begins recording statements from families
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal is treating enforced disappearances during the Awami League regime as systematic crimes against humanity.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has begun recording statements from the families of 55 people who were subjected to enforced disappearance during the Awami League regime and have not returned.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that investigators have confirmed more than 251 people were subjected to enforced disappearance and never returned home.

The tribunal is treating these disappearances as widespread and systematic acts that may amount to crimes against humanity, noting that the victims were picked up in a similar pattern by law enforcement agencies.
Investigators are collecting statements, documents, photographs, and writ petitions to establish the pattern of disappearance and identify the perpetrators.
Around 18 investigating officers are working to complete the investigation by the end of the year so that the trial can begin.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam has urged the government to strengthen security for the families of the victims and witnesses, citing concerns that some suspects may attempt to sabotage the investigation.
Mayer Daak coordinator Sanjida Islam Tulee expressed hope that the investigation would now gain momentum after families had waited for justice for over a decade.
caption:
Over 251 people vanished without a trace. Now, the ICT is treating these disappearances as crimes against humanity.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has begun recording statements from the families of 55 people who were subjected to enforced disappearance during the Awami League regime and have not returned.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam stated that investigators have confirmed more than 251 people were subjected to enforced disappearance and never returned home.

The tribunal is treating these disappearances as widespread and systematic acts that may amount to crimes against humanity, noting that the victims were picked up in a similar pattern by law enforcement agencies.

Investigators are collecting statements, documents, photographs, and writ petitions to establish the pattern of disappearance and identify the perpetrators.

Around 18 investigating officers are working to complete the investigation by the end of the year so that the trial can begin.

Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam has urged the government to strengthen security for the families of the victims and witnesses, citing concerns that some suspects may attempt to sabotage the investigation.

Mayer Daak coordinator Sanjida Islam Tulee expressed hope that the investigation would now gain momentum after families had waited for justice for over a decade.

#Bangladesh #ICT #HumanRights #Justice #MayerDaak

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
